drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Counsel,

Attached is our proposed draft for discussion. We have specified a USD 35 million purchase price, clarified closing mechanics, and proposed customary qualifications and limitations on the Seller's representations and indemnity obligations. We suggest working next toward agreed disclosure schedules and closing deliverables.

The draft remains subject to our client's review and approval.

edits.text: 1. PURCHASE PRICE. The aggregate purchase price for the Shares shall be USD 35,000,000 (the "Purchase Price"), payable by the Buyer to the Seller at Closing by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated by the Seller, without setoff or deduction except as required by applicable law.

2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur within thirty days of signing, subject to receipt of required regulatory approvals and satisfaction or written waiver by the entitled party of the closing conditions expressly agreed in this Agreement. At Closing, the Seller shall deliver instruments transferring the Shares against simultaneous payment of the Purchase Price. Any extension shall require the parties' written agreement.

3. REPRESENTATIONS. Except as disclosed in disclosure schedules to be agreed and attached to this Agreement at signing, the Seller represents that the financial statements delivered to the Buyer fairly present, in all material respects, the financial position and results of operations of the Company for the periods covered, in accordance with the accounting principles identified therein, consistently applied, subject, in the case of interim statements, to normal year-end adjustments and the absence of footnotes.

4. INDEMNITY. Following Closing, the Seller shall indemnify the Buyer for actual, direct losses resulting from a breach of the Seller's express representations or covenants in this Agreement. Claims for breach of representations must be notified in reasonable detail within twelve months after Closing. The Seller shall be liable for such claims only to the extent their aggregate amount exceeds one percent of the Purchase Price, and aggregate liability for such claims shall not exceed ten percent of the Purchase Price. No recovery shall be available for matters fairly disclosed in this Agreement or the disclosure schedules, amounts recovered from insurance or third parties, or duplicate losses. The Buyer shall take commercially reasonable steps to mitigate losses. Except for fraud by the Seller and claims for specific performance, this Section shall be the Buyer's exclusive remedy following Closing.

drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Thank you for your proposal. The Seller cannot accept USD 28 million. To bridge the gap, we propose USD 32 million together with the attached package: expanded Seller representations, 18-month survival for general representations, a 15% general indemnity cap, a 0.75% deductible basket and a 5% escrow credited against—not additional to—the applicable liability caps. We have also provided separate treatment for title, authority, taxes and actual Seller fraud. Diligence and disclosure schedules should be completed before signing, with objective closing conditions rather than an open-ended diligence condition. These concessions are offered as an integrated package, subject to agreement on the definitive documentation.

edits.text: 1. PURCHASE PRICE. The aggregate purchase price for the Shares shall be USD 32,000,000 (the "Purchase Price"). At Closing, the Buyer shall pay ninety-five percent of the Purchase Price to the Seller by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated by the Seller and deposit the remaining five percent with an independent escrow agent under an escrow agreement agreed at signing. Payments shall be made without setoff or deduction except as required by applicable law. The escrow shall secure claims under Section 4 and shall not increase any applicable liability cap.

2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur within thirty days of signing, subject to receipt of required regulatory approvals, absence of any legal prohibition on Closing, the accuracy of each party's representations at Closing (except for representations expressly made as of another date), and performance in all material respects of each party's pre-Closing covenants. For purposes of the accuracy condition, inaccuracies shall be disregarded unless, individually or in the aggregate, they materially impair the relevant party's ability to consummate the transaction or, in the case of Company representations, have a material adverse effect on the Company taken as a whole. Conditions may be waived in writing only by the party entitled to their benefit. The Buyer shall complete its diligence, and the parties shall agree and attach the disclosure schedules, before signing; satisfactory diligence shall not be a post-signing closing condition. At Closing, the Seller shall deliver instruments transferring the Shares against simultaneous payment and funding of the escrow under Section 1. Any extension shall require the parties' written agreement.

3. REPRESENTATIONS. Except as fairly disclosed in disclosure schedules agreed and attached at signing, the Seller represents that: (a) the Seller has authority to execute and perform this Agreement, which constitutes its binding obligation, subject to applicable insolvency laws and equitable principles; (b) the Seller owns the Shares free of liens and may transfer them to the Buyer, and the capitalization schedule accurately states the Company's issued equity and outstanding rights to acquire equity; (c) the Company is duly organized and validly existing; (d) the financial statements delivered to the Buyer fairly present, in all material respects, the Company's financial position and results for the periods covered in accordance with the accounting principles identified therein, consistently applied, subject for interim statements to normal year-end adjustments and absence of footnotes; (e) the Company is in compliance in all material respects with applicable laws and holds the material permits necessary for its business; (f) the material contracts identified in the schedules are in force and neither the Company nor, to the Seller's knowledge, any counterparty is in material default; (g) there is no pending or, to the Seller's knowledge, threatened material litigation against the Company; (h) the Company has timely filed all material tax returns and paid all material taxes due; (i) the Company owns or has valid rights to use the material assets and intellectual property necessary to conduct its business; and (j) since the date of its latest financial statements, the Company has operated in the ordinary course in all material respects and has not suffered a material adverse effect. 'Seller's knowledge' means the actual knowledge of the Seller's personnel identified in the schedules after reasonable inquiry of the managers responsible for the relevant subject matter. A disclosure qualifies another representation only where its relevance to that representation is reasonably apparent on its face.

4. INDEMNITY. Following Closing, the Seller shall indemnify the Buyer for actual, direct losses resulting from breach of the Seller's express representations or covenants in this Agreement and for unpaid taxes of the Company attributable to periods ending on or before Closing, including the pre-Closing portion of any straddle period. General representation claims must be notified in reasonable detail, describing the factual basis and a good-faith estimate of loss to the extent reasonably ascertainable, within eighteen months after Closing. For such claims, the Seller shall be liable only for aggregate losses exceeding 0.75% of the Purchase Price, and only for the excess; aggregate liability shall not exceed 15% of the Purchase Price. Claims relating to title to the Shares, capitalization or Seller authority may be notified within six years after Closing; tax claims may be notified until sixty days after expiration of the applicable statutory limitation period. Those claims are not subject to the basket or general cap, but, together with all other claims under this Agreement, shall not exceed the Purchase Price, except in the case of actual fraud committed by the Seller. Covenants survive according to their terms, with claims to be notified within twelve months after the applicable performance deadline. A timely notified claim survives until finally resolved. No recovery shall be available for matters fairly disclosed in this Agreement or the disclosure schedules, amounts actually recovered from insurance or third parties net of reasonable recovery costs, duplicate losses, or punitive damages except to the extent payable to a third party. The Buyer shall take commercially reasonable steps to mitigate losses. The escrow shall be the first source of recovery for indemnity claims, without limiting recovery from the Seller within the applicable caps. At eighteen months after Closing, the escrow balance shall be released to the Seller, less amounts reasonably reserved for timely notified unresolved claims; each reserve shall be released promptly following resolution and payment of the relevant claim. Except for actual fraud committed by the Seller and claims for specific performance, this Section shall be the Buyer's exclusive remedy following Closing.
